## Validation Notes

**Iteration 1 (failed) → Iteration 2 (passed).** The first draft carried the source brief's
technical specificity verbatim and failed CHK001, CHK008, and CHK016: it named concrete
endpoint paths, a specific vector index name, specific hosted-embedding model names,
environment-variable names, and asserted success criteria in terms of specific
infrastructure ("system starts successfully via Docker Compose", "PostgreSQL migrations
apply cleanly", "Pinecone index `enterprise-knowledge` can be initialized"). Those criteria
were not verifiable without implementation knowledge, which is exactly what CHK008 prohibits.

The spec was rewritten to express requirements as observable capability and user outcome.
Infrastructure was re-expressed by role — "hosted embedding and vector-retrieval service",
"registry of record", "single-command local environment" — and moved out of the requirements
and success criteria entirely.

**Two vendor references are intentionally retained**, and are the only proper nouns in the
requirement and assumption text:

- **Groq** (Input, Assumptions) — explicitly mandated by the user as the default language
  model provider. Recorded as a *product decision*, not an implementation technique, and
  paired with a provider-neutrality requirement so the pipeline is not coupled to it.
- **The destination repository** (Input, Assumptions) — `github.com/Saif-Ali-109/Enterprise-Intelligence-RAG`,
  confirmed empty and public. Retained because the brief's licensing and independence
  obligations are meaningless without naming where the work is published.

Both live in `**Input**` and `## Assumptions`. Neither appears in any functional requirement
or success criterion. The mandated technology stack is deliberately **not** restated here; it
is already binding via the ratified constitution (Principle VII and the Additional Constraints
section) and belongs to `/speckit.plan`.

**CHK011 scope boundary** is explicit: the release excludes authoring or editing documentation,
write-back to external systems, non-English corpora, live-data retrieval, end-user accounts and
multi-tenancy, and transport encryption. The 50–100 page corpus ceiling is stated as a deliberate
quality-over-volume decision rather than an oversight.

**CHK007 / CHK015** are satisfied by 20 numeric success criteria, of which 9 are pass/fail
gates on measured quality (SC-001 through SC-009). Per the user's decision these are enforced as
gates: an evaluation run below threshold MUST be reported as a failing run (FR-041), not quietly
displayed as a pass. Two criteria are deliberately absolute-zero targets — SC-008 (zero fabricated
facts or citations on unsupported questions) and SC-009 (zero invalid citation identifiers) —
because a retrieval system that fabricates is worse than one that abstains, and both are
deterministically checkable rather than judgement calls.

**CHK010** covers 16 edge cases including the ones most likely to be skipped: empty corpus
(distinguishing "nothing indexed" from "nothing relevant"), duplicate content, provider outage,
model-emitted phantom citations, prompt-injection content in a user's question, and a source
whose pages have all been deleted.

**Item status**: All 16 items pass. Three user decisions were resolved before drafting
(scope granularity, numeric quality gates, licence) and are recorded in Assumptions.

- Items marked incomplete require spec updates before `/speckit.clarify` or `/speckit.plan`
- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit.implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit.specify` and `/speckit.clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
